input.question: How was German culture effected by the years between the end of WWII and reunification?
input.ground_truth: I'm not a historian, but a German. So in fact there were two countries, DDR and BRD, or East Germany and West Germany. But in both countries the people were mostly german and spoke german. So there was no big cultural difference, except maybe food. Regarding patriotism: There was just a minority of people who were against a unification of the DDR and the BRD. The people were smart enough to see that the communist part of the world was crumbling and they wanted to be free. After the unification background checks of the administrative elite were executed. So you didn't really have supporters of the old regime in important positions anymore. I don't know if this answers your questions.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How was German culture effected by the years between the end of WWII and reunification?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine Germany was like a big toy that got broken into two pieces after a really big fight (that’s World War II). For a long time after the fight, one side of the toy (West Germany) got lots of new toys and candy (money and help from other countries), so the kids there could play and have fun.

But the other side of the toy (East Germany) didn’t get as many new things. The grown-ups there told the kids what to do and what to play with, and they couldn’t go wherever they wanted. So the kids on that side had to play by different rules and didn’t have as much fun.

When the toy finally got put back together (that’s called reunification), the kids from both sides got to play together again. But it was a little weird at first, because they played different games and had different toys for so long. Some kids were happy, but some were sad or confused because things were so different.

So, the years between the end of the big fight and putting the toy back together changed how the German kids played, what they learned, and how they felt about each other.
